tools.name: list_boards
tools.title: List the boards
tools.description: List the project's boards. Call it first: the other tools take a board id. No input, no credentials. Returns `project` (the folder the board has open), `head` (the ledger's latest line) and `boards`, each with `board` (its id), `title`, `seq` (its own latest line) and `locked: true` when the person has locked it (no writes).

tools.name: get_board
tools.title: Read a board as it is now
tools.description: Read one board as it is now. Pass `board`. Returns `head`, the View (regions, nodes and links; meaning only, no coordinates), `state` (the person's answers on each card, pins and modes) and `versions` (each card's latest version), cards keyed by number as a string. Cards are numbered from 1 per board in draw order, never reused; retired cards are left out. When agents write to the board, also open grant `requests` and each region's `holders` (left out when empty). `locked: true`: read it, but don't write (every write answers `locked`). For one node's history, use `show_node`.

tools.name: show_node
tools.title: Read one node with its history
tools.description: Read one card with its history. Pass `board` and `n`, the card's number on that board; `linked: true` adds the nodes linked to it, one hop away. Returns every version, the person's notes, replies, proposals, the park bundle if any, links, its container (`region`) and the person's size; a retired card still answers, with `retired`. Read it before you answer a note or redraw a card, to build on the latest version.

n.description: The card's number on this board (1, 2, 3... in the order drawn).

linked.description: True also returns the nodes linked to this one.

tools.name: show_container
tools.title: Read one container with its history
tools.description: Read one container (region) with its history. Pass `board` and `region`. Returns the region, the agents that hold it (`holders`, empty on an old region) and every node it has held, with every version and note. Read it before you write to a container or ask for a grant on it.

tools.name: show_layout
tools.title: Read how one container is arranged
tools.description: Read how one container is arranged, as structure only. Pass `board` and `region`. Returns the mode and card widths in effect, each card's column and row (and lane in `lanes` mode) by card number, how many of its links cross another, and how many cells are empty. Call it once after you first draw a `flow` or `lanes` container, and redraw if it reads badly (many crossings or empty cells); not after every write. `write_board` does not return it.

tools.name: list_open
tools.title: List the open cards
tools.description: List a board's open cards. Pass `board`. Returns every question, decision or action the person has not marked ✓ or ✗ (a note never answers a card), and every card waiting for you, each with its latest `ver`, `status`, `pending` (waiting for your answer: an unanswered note, or Later with no park bundle) and `unseen` (newer than the person last saw, or your answer cleared it and they have not looked since). With your secret, only the containers you hold, so you never answer another agent's cards.

tools.name: check_responses
tools.title: Wait for the person's answers
tools.description: Read what the person did on a board after a ledger position, including answers to your grant requests. Pass `board` and `after` (the `head` you last saw; 0 for all); optional `limit`, and `wait` (0-60 seconds) to hold until the person presses Send or answers a request. Returns `responses`, `head` and `more`; a wait that times out returns `{ responses: [], head }`. A note comes as the `comment` act that made it (`context` on an old More context note) with its latest text and kind, again whenever the person edits it; a note removed before you saw it never appears, and `note-remove` appears only for one you may have read. Each batch, up to its Send, is sorted by card number: a note on several cards at its lowest card, a note on a container at its lowest card, several acts on one card in the order made. ✓ reads `check` and ✗ reads `cross`: the person's marks on a card that asks, meaning what your card asks; a note never answers a card. Each card's ✓, ✗, Later and clear (`reopen`) fold to its latest, shown only when it differs from how it stood at `after` (✓ then cleared shows nothing). No state is kept for you: pass back the `head` you got. `more: true`: `limit` cut the list in ledger order, so read again at once with `after` set to the highest `seq` in `responses`. With your secret, only the containers you hold.

after.description: Return what came after this ledger `seq` (default 0: from the start). Pass the `head` you last saw.

limit.description: How many to return at most (default 100, at most 500).

wait.description: Seconds (0-60) to wait for the person's Send or an answer to a request; 0 answers at once.

tools.name: join
tools.title: Join as an agent
tools.description: Join the project as an agent, once. Pass a short `label`, such as "Pricing chat". Returns your `agent` id, your `secret` and `project`, the folder the board has open: check it is the folder you work in. Save `agent` and `secret` in your durable notes now: a context compaction loses them and the secret cannot be read again. Send the secret as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` on your writes. Joining grants nothing: draw a new board of your own, or call `request_grant` with just `board` for a board another agent made. A write that answers `not-authenticated`: join again and ask for your grants again. A call that answers `wrong-folder`: the board has another folder open, so stop, tell the person, and do not join. The one write that needs no credentials.

label.description: A short name for this chat or agent, such as "Pricing chat". The person sees it when you ask for access.

tools.name: request_grant
tools.title: Ask for write access to a board or a container
tools.description: Ask the person for write access to a board, or to one container on it. Before you write on a board you did not create, call it with just `board`; for another agent's container, with `board` and `region`. Call it once when `write_board` answers `needs-grant`, naming what that answer names, with a `reason` the person can decide on; then wait in `check_responses` and resend the same items with the same keys. A locked board takes no request (`locked`, 423). Returns `request`, the request's `seq` (the person's answer names it); an open request for the same thing comes back with `replayed: true`, and `{ held: true }` when you already hold it.

board.description: The board you need to write to, or that holds the container.

region.description: The container (region) you need. Leave it out to ask for the whole board.

reason.description: Why you need write access, so the person can decide.

key.description: Retry key, per agent across the project.

tools.name: write_board
tools.title: Write to a board
tools.description: Write to one board: draw boards, regions, nodes and links, and answer the person with replies, proposals and park bundles. For a new board, choose its id yourself and start with a `board` item. Pass `items` (1-200), run in order, each with a `type`: `board`, `region`, `node`, `link`, `unlink`, `reply`, `propose`, `park`, `retire` or `append`. `n`, `from` and `to` name a card by its number on this board (from 1, in draw order) or by `{ key }` of the item that drew it. Give every item a `key` so a retry never writes twice, and a node update `base` (the `ver` you read) so a stale edit fails with `conflict`. Kinds `question`, `decision` and `action` ask the person for ✓ or ✗; kind `app` shows an app you built (`app: { id }`, from `list_apps`). Region modes: `grid`, `flow` (follows the links), `lanes`, `radial`, `column` (top to bottom) and `row` (left to right); `widths` is `match` or `own`. `append { n, text }` adds to the end of a card's body as a new version. `retire { n }` or `retire { region }` takes a card, or a container and its cards, off the board for good; answer a card waiting on you first. You cannot answer a card: `propose` its ✓ (`check`) or ✗ (`cross`) and the person answers; a proposal on an older version can't be accepted, so propose again after you change the card. On a board you did not create, call `request_grant` first: an item there fails with `needs-grant` naming the board (or the board and region, in another agent's container). Only a board's creator writes its `board` item again. Returns one result per item, `head`, and `pending` (cards waiting for your answer).

tools.name: list_apps
tools.title: List the apps in this folder
tools.description: List the apps in this folder, to draw one on a card or see what to fix. Apps live in `.visionboard/apps/<id>/` (the Vision Board skill says what goes there). Returns each app's `id` and `state`: `ready`, `needs-approval` (it has tools the person has not allowed at this version; `changed: true` when they allowed an earlier one), `invalid` (fix its `problems`), `broken` (its tools crashed too often; change the code to try again) or `missing` (a card names it, but there is no folder); and the manifest's `title`, `version` and panel `size`, its `tools` by name, and `hash`, the version of its code, with `allowed: true` once the person allowed that hash. Only the person allows an app, on its card. Draw one as a `node` item of kind `app` with `app: { id, w?, h? }`, the panel's size in px. Needs your secret.
